justifications.c1: Independent per-incident figures exist (Taw & Torridge £25.5k fine + >£80k costs, search-confirmed; DJM £19.6k; Cavalier £3.9k) but none is a separator overflow at a depot (tank/pump leaks, delivery spills), so the money is not tied to this specific failure.
justifications.c2: Only national aggregates (EA 499 serious incidents 2015; ~800 oil incidents/yr) and six-monthly servicing from a vendor guide; researcher recorded no per-depot or per-separator failure rate.
justifications.c3: Paid contracted servicing/emptying is documented (Adler & Allan, GPT, CSG, Bay Oils; public tenders on Find a Tender) with a six-monthly cadence, but every price is quote-only and the cadence source is a vendor.
justifications.c4: Alarm-fitting requirement since 2021 is supply-side only (Defra/BIVDA item search-confirmed; SPEL vendor); GPP 3 is non-regulatory in England; no operator duty to keep records and no insurer condition found; enforcement shown is for general pollution offences, not separator records.
justifications.c5: SHEQ/depot manager adverts cited, but none mention interceptors and the researcher found no budget authority for drainage/separator spend.
justifications.c6: Interceptor contractors (Adler & Allan, GPT, CSG, Bay Oils) visit every separator and test alarms as part of service, but no evidence they resell or bundle remote monitoring.
justifications.c7: Crowded: Kingspan/Klargester alarm £359 ex VAT (search-confirmed), Labkotec idOil incl. battery 3G, Aquasentry web monitor, Afriso cloud, GSM/solar units; the silt/empty-on-demand gap is asserted, not evidenced.
justifications.c8: Red flags: Afriso's separator alarm is Ex-rated (ATEX may be needed), oil/water interface probe is a specialist element (components €470-€500 each), underground chamber RF; no BOM found.
justifications.c9: Six-monthly service cycle and alarm testing recur, but no statutory record retention and no UK subscription price for remote separator monitoring was found.
justifications.c10: EA press release plus trade press (Route One, Commercial Motor) and contractor marketing; all concern diesel leaks generally, not separator overflow; no forum complaints found.

weakest: None of the cited prosecutions was caused by an overfull or unalarmed separator, and remote oil/high-level alarms (including battery/cellular) are already sold by several incumbents.
